## Section IV: Essay 10 marks

**Write an essay of 250 to 300 words on any one o4thefollowing topics. If you choose the article or the letter your name should be Ngupeyu and your address Lycée de Yom.,**

1. Write a letter to your friend who is out of the country. Tell him/her about the changes that have taken place in the country in this year 2000.
2. Write an article to the editor of the "Zoom" newspaper on health problems in your town.
3. Machines are man's enemies and/or his friends. Discuss.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un sujet de type "Discuss" (ici, "Machines are man's enemies and/or his friends") est un essai discursif : il exige une introduction qui reformule le sujet et annonce le plan, un développement équilibré qui présente **les deux points de vue** (les machines comme ennemies, puis comme amies, ou l'inverse), chaque paragraphe étant structuré autour d'une idée principale appuyée par un exemple concret, et une conclusion qui prend position ou nuance le débat sans se contenter de répéter l'introduction. Le nombre de mots imposé (250 à 300) doit être respecté : trop court, l'essai est pénalisé pour développement insuffisant ; trop long, le candidat perd du temps sur les autres sections.

**Sujet traité : "Machines are man's enemies and/or his friends. Discuss."**

*(Modèle rédigé en anglais, la langue de production exigée par l'épreuve elle-même ; environ 270 mots.)*

> Since the industrial revolution, machines have transformed the way human beings live and work. Whether they should be regarded as man's friends, his enemies, or both at once, is a question worth discussing.
>
> On the one hand, machines can rightly be seen as enemies. In factories, robots and automated systems have replaced thousands of workers, leaving many people unemployed and struggling to support their families. Machines can also be dangerous: industrial accidents, plane crashes and car accidents cause the death of many people every year. Furthermore, an excessive dependence on machines makes human beings lazier, both physically and mentally, since many tasks that used to require effort and thinking are now performed automatically.
>
> On the other hand, machines remain, in most respects, man's friends. They have considerably reduced the burden of hard physical labour: washing machines, tractors and computers save time and energy that can be devoted to more rewarding activities. In medicine, machines such as scanners and life-support systems save countless lives every day. In addition, machines have made communication and travel easier, bringing people who live far apart closer together.
>
> In conclusion, machines are neither purely enemies nor purely friends: everything depends on how they are used. A tool that saves a patient's life in a hospital and a machine gun used in a war are both machines, yet they serve entirely opposite purposes. It is therefore man, and not the machine itself, who decides whether technology becomes a source of progress or a source of harm. Used wisely, machines remain one of humanity's greatest allies.

### Piège à éviter
Un essai "Discuss" qui ne développe qu'un seul point de vue (uniquement "amies" ou uniquement "ennemies") est pénalisé, même si l'argumentation est excellente : la consigne "and/or" attend explicitement une discussion des deux faces du sujet, pas un plaidoyer à sens unique.

### Conseil
Compte approximativement tes mots par paragraphe plutôt qu'à la fin seulement (par exemple, environ 50 mots pour l'introduction, 90 pour chaque partie du développement, 40 pour la conclusion) : cela évite de découvrir, une fois l'essai terminé, qu'il est bien trop court ou trop long par rapport aux 250-300 mots exigés.
